description: FAQ accordion using native HTML details/summary elements. Zero JavaScript required. Each item has a question and an HTML answer. Emits a FAQPage JSON-LD structured-data block alongside the visible markup, zero-config with no toggle: an entry whose question or answer is empty is skipped, as is one whose value is damaged (a non-scalar, or an entry that is not an object), and no block is emitted at all when no entry survives. REBUILT ON THE UNIVERSAL DESIGN CONTRACT (v2): it declares no style slots. Every designable value — colour, type, spacing, border, shadow, size, motion — is set through the `udc` map on the band, per role. See docs/v2/BUILD-SPEC-sprint0.md §3.

id.description: Optional HTML id attribute for anchor linking (e.g. navigation anchors). Also becomes the component's stable id.

title.description: Section heading displayed above the FAQ list.

title_accent.description: Optional exact substring of title to render in an accent color. Must match title exactly (case-sensitive) or it is ignored.

eyebrow.description: Optional short kicker/label rendered as a pill above the title.

items.description: Array of FAQ items. Each item: { question: string, answer: string (HTML allowed) }.

question.description: The question text shown in the accordion summary. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

answer.description: The answer body. Rich HTML (sanitized via wp_kses_post): block-level markup, lists, and links are allowed.

retired_props._note: Props this component declared on 1.x that the v2 rebuild retired (#1046). Each value names the v2 surface that replaced it, so a refusal can offer a route instead of a list of live prop names. Guarded by SchemaValidationTest, which fails in BOTH directions: a key here that still exists in props, or a route naming a role this component does not declare, is a test failure rather than a message that lies.
retired_props.theme: the `_band` role — and it takes MORE than a background, which is why the route names three groups rather than one. MEASURED, all three values, before the prop went: `default` painted `@color-surface` with NO border on any edge; `muted` painted the same fill PLUS a 1px solid `@color-border` rule top and bottom (it emitted the legacy `faq--dark` class, #570 DG-4); `inverted` swapped the fill for `@color-bg-inverted` and re-coloured the heading to `@color-bg`, leaving the question, the answer and the accordion items untouched because the items keep their own light fill. So: the tone is `background.fill`; the `muted` framing is `border.width-top` / `width-bottom` = "1px" with `style-top` / `style-bottom` = "solid" and `color` = "@color-border"; the `inverted` ink is `typography.color` on `_band` (the `heading` role follows it through `currentColor`). `dark` was NOT an accepted input value and is not part of this route: it was removed at #605 and `pp_theme_class()` clamped it to `default`.

_band.description: The band itself — the <section>. Set the band's own background here to make a dark or tinted band; the v1 `theme` prop is gone because a preset bundle of colours is exactly what the UDC expresses directly. THE DEFAULTS ARE WHAT v1's UNTHEMED BAND RENDERED, measured in Chromium at 375/768/1280 rather than read off the stylesheet: a surface fill and the shared band rhythm, with NO border on any edge. That last part is the difference from cta, whose `_band` draws a 1px rule top and bottom: v1's `.faq` declared no border at all — the framing rules belonged to `.faq--dark`, the retired `theme: "muted"` variant — so silence here is the faithful port, and the issue-332 border-immunity baseline in `pp-v1` has nothing of faq's to erase. A band background image is `background.image` (an attachment id) with `background.overlay` for the scrim, a capability faq never had on v1, where the component declared no `background_image` prop at all. SETTING `typography.color` HERE RE-INKS THE HEADING, AND THE HEADING IS NOT THE WHOLE BAND. The `heading` role follows this write through `currentColor`. The `question`, `answer` and `empty` roles do NOT, because each pins a measured v1 value, and a pinned role default is a DIRECT declaration that an inherited band colour can never beat. The three are pinned for TWO different reasons and need two different remedies: `question` and `answer` sit inside the `item` panel, which stays light by default (see the `item` role), while `empty` sits on the band fill itself and is the one a correct dark-panel write leaves behind (see the `empty` role). A dark band therefore costs this write PLUS one per role whose text it must reach.

eyebrow.description: The kicker pill above the heading. Measured byte-identical to cta's, section's and hero's eyebrow roles, and declared per-schema rather than extracted for the reason #1023 recorded: role declaration is data the engine shares, so a fourth copy of the same values is the contract working rather than duplication to factor out.

heading.description: The band heading (an <h2>). ITS `typography.color` IS `currentColor`, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE LITERAL v1 DECLARATION rather than a transcription of it. v1's rule was `color: var(--faq-heading-color, var(--pp-faq-heading-theme-color, var(--color-text)))` — a pinned literal, not cta's `inherit` — so the literally faithful port would be `@color-text`. The reason it is not: the only way v1 could render a dark faq band was `theme: "inverted"`, which supplied `--pp-faq-heading-theme-color`, and that prop is retired. Carrying the literal forward would pin the heading against the one band shape v2 newly makes easy — measured, `@color-text` on an authored `@color-bg-inverted` band is 1.006:1, invisible, the same defect #1026 shipped and corrected. `currentColor` in the `color` property is defined to mean `inherit`, so an authored `_band` -> `typography.color` reaches this heading (17.54:1 on that same band) and an authored value on this role still wins. It is IDENTICAL to `@color-text` on every band v1 could actually express, which is why only a dark-band read distinguishes the two. ITS WEIGHT AND LEADING ARE RESTATED and its family, tracking and `text-wrap` are not: the weight and leading come from `main > .faq .faq__heading` rules that exist ONLY inside the two media queries, so dropping them would restyle every tier, while the other three come from base.css's shared `h1`-`h6` rule and restating a global value would move it to the unlayered tier and beat that rule in every state.

heading-accent.description: The accented substring inside the heading, rendered only when title_accent occurs in title exactly.

list.description: The accordion stack. It owns the gap BETWEEN items; the column direction is layout geometry and stays in the stylesheet. The gap is the only design value on this element, which is why this role carries three groups rather than the usual six.

item.description: One accordion item — the <details> box. ITS FILL IS `@color-bg` AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THE INK ABOVE IT. v1 deliberately kept items light even on an inverted band (the same choice grid makes for its cards), and that is why the `question` and `answer` roles pin their colours instead of following the band: on v1's own dark band their measured ink was unchanged, because the panel under them was still light. THE CONSEQUENCE IS YOURS TO CARRY IN v2: if you darken this fill, set `question` -> `typography.color` and `answer` -> `typography.color` in the same write, or the text keeps a dark value on a dark panel. `empty` IS NOT PART OF THIS PAIR and this write does not fix it: `.faq__empty` renders as a direct child of `.container`, on the band fill, never inside this panel — so darkening this fill cannot strand it, and re-inking these two cannot rescue it. Its own pinned colour is a separate obligation, recorded on that role. `overflow: hidden` is structural — it is what clips the open answer to this box's radius.

question.description: The <summary> row at REST — the closed state only. Its positional twin is `question-open`, which owns the expanded state, and the two are set together or not at all: a colour set here alone reverts the moment a reader opens the item, because the open role's selector carries one more compound and outranks this one. THE SAME RANKING APPLIES TO STATES, and it is the part that is easy to miss: a `:hover` or `:focus-visible` map on THIS role reaches a closed row and not an open one, because an open row is matched by a heavier selector. Set the state on `question-open` too when it must survive opening. Its size and leading are breakpoint maps and its weight is a flat 560, all three READ FROM THE BROWSER rather than from the stylesheet: the base rule declares `font-weight: 600`, which never renders, because `main > .faq .faq__question` overrides it inside both media queries and the two partition every width. The 44px touch target, the pointer cursor, the marker suppression and the `transition` property list stay structural; `motion` -> `transition-duration` retunes the timing of that transition without widening what it animates.

question-open.description: The <summary> row of an OPEN item — the accordion's expand affordance, and the only role in this theme whose selector is an ancestor state. Ruling A3 defers ancestor states as a value DIMENSION, so this is expressed the way nav's `link-current` expresses the current page: as its own role with its own selector, which is what the role-selector charset was widened for — at #994 for the child combinator, at #1046 for the two bracket characters. Measured with a real pointer click at three viewports: the resting `@color-text` becomes `@color-accent`, 5.43:1 against the item's own fill, and the disclosure chevron follows for free because it is drawn with currentColor borders — which is also why the chevron needs no role of its own: its INK is already authorable through this role and through `question`, and only its box and stroke are stated defaults. THE CHEVRON ITSELF IS NOT AUTHORABLE — it is a `::after` pseudo-element and ruling A3 defers those, so its 10px box, its 2px stroke and its 45deg/225deg rotation stay structural, the same classification nav's chevron rotation takes. This role's default outranks an authored resting colour on `question` (one more compound in the selector), which reproduces v1's positional-twin behaviour exactly: set both or neither.

answer.description: The answer body, revealed when the item opens. Its colour and leading are breakpoint maps and its size and weight are flat, every one of them measured rather than declared: v1 gave the phone tier `@color-muted` from an unscoped base rule and the two wider tiers `@color-text-secondary` from a rule inside `@media (min-width: 768px)`, which is the #1023 media-scope trap in its exact shape — carrying the desktop literal unconditionally would have restyled every phone render of the answer, and dropping the weight and leading with the rules that carried them would have restyled every tier. IT CARRIES NO MEASURE, deliberately: v1 declared `max-width: var(--faq-body-measure, none)` and rendered `none`, so the faithful port is silence. LINKS INSIDE THE ANSWER ARE NOT A ROLE: measured, a body link renders `@color-accent` underlined, byte-identical to what base.css gives every anchor, and a role block is emitted unlayered — restating those values would outrank the shared premium button rules for an author-written `<a class="btn">` inside an answer, which is the #545 defect reintroduced through a role selector (the reasoning cta recorded for `body-link` at #1026). An authored colour on this role still wins, which is what a darkened item needs.

empty.description: The "No questions yet." line a band with no items renders. ITS COLOUR IS A ROLE DEFAULT AND THE MARKUP LOST A UTILITY CLASS TO MAKE THAT TRUE. v1 rendered this grey by putting `text-muted` on the element, which hardcodes `--color-muted` from utilities.css in `@layer pp-v1` — and a class like that WINS over an authored colour, so keeping it would have made the one line on the band nobody can re-ink the empty state. footer's rebuild met the identical case at #994 and ruled it the same way: the template dropped the class so the role governs. `@color-muted` is therefore the measured v1 value carried as a default rather than a value left in the stylesheet, and an author who sets a colour here now gets it — which is exactly what the utility class made impossible. READ THAT LITERALLY: it is the write aimed at THIS role that lands. THE `_band` WRITE DOES NOT REACH THIS LINE. A role default emits as `[data-pp-component="faq"] .faq__empty{color:var(--color-muted);}` — a direct declaration, unlayered — while `_band` -> `typography.color` emits on the band root and reaches descendants only by INHERITANCE, which a direct declaration always beats. Measured: with a `_band` fill of `#0f172a` and `typography.color` set light, this line still resolves to `--color-muted` (`#5e6677`) at 3.10:1, under the 4.5:1 AA floor for body text. So a dark band WITH NO ITEMS needs two writes, `_band` and `empty`, the same way a dark panel needs `question` and `answer`. This is not a regression — v1's `text-muted` was stranded on `.faq--inverted` in the identical way — but v2 is the first version where the fix is one write away, so the obligation is named here rather than left to be discovered.
